subject: Engineering decisions
title: Flow tests with a real dependency move to the integration tier (owner, 25 Oct)
question: What was measured for Flow tests with a real dependency move to the integration tier (owner, 25 Oct)?
workload: Flow tests with a real dependency move to the integration tier (owner, 25 Oct)
method: Transcribed from the cited historical record. Units and precision follow the source.
finding: CI: `cargo-integration` Nx task per crate with `tests/integration.rs` (one test thread); `wf test plan` plans `test:integration` and the crates' integration in `service-e2e-tests` (after the CLIs are built and the services deployed), not `flow-tests`; the job installs Chromium and ffmpeg, publishes the integration run bundles, and its timeout grew from 10 to 35 minutes.

rows: - CI: `cargo-integration` Nx task per crate with `tests/integration.rs` (one test thread); `wf test plan` plans `test:integration` and the crates' integration in `service-e2e-tests` (after the CLIs are built and the services deployed), not `flow-tests`; the job installs Chromium and ffmpeg, publishes the integration run bundles, and its timeout grew from 10 to 35 minutes.

- Not proven: that the earlier Chromium timeouts came from parallel launches (the error only said `goto` did not finish in 30 s). Moving the tests removes real browsers from `flow-tests`; the first `service-e2e-tests` run measures them.
